name: Lee Chou Sarn
current_role: No public executive role found; family linked to NagaCorp (Cambodia casino operator)
profile: Lee Chou Sarn is listed as the (first) wife of the late Tan Sri Chen Lip Keong, founder of Hong Kong-listed NagaCorp, which runs NagaWorld in Phnom Penh. Chen died in December 2023; his controlling stake sits in the Sakai family trust and their son Chen Yiy Fon became NagaCorp CEO. Her wealth listing appears to derive from this family holding.
interesting_fact: Her three sons with Chen Lip Keong (Yiy Fon, Yiy Hwan and Yipern) inherited NagaCorp interests; Chen Yiy Fon was named NagaCorp CEO in December 2023.
notes: Almost no public footprint; only appears as spouse in Chen Lip Keong's Wikipedia infobox and press on his succession. Not a NagaCorp director. Any approach would go through NagaCorp (nagacorp.com) corporate channels; the family succession has been contentious, so avoid that topic.

name: Shen Bo
profile: Bo Shen co-founded Fenbushi Capital in 2015, one of Asia's earliest blockchain-focused VC firms (Vitalik Buterin was an early co-founder), and has been an early backer of Ethereum-ecosystem and Web3 projects. A Georgia Tech-trained engineer, he spent years in US and Chinese finance before moving into crypto, and was a co-founder of Invictus Innovations, the team behind BitShares.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he joined Hedera Hashgraph as a strategic advisor focused on Asia-Pacific growth, shortly after its mainnet launch.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto, he earned a master's in systems engineering at Georgia Tech and worked at Raymond James Financial (1993-98) as a financial consultant and VP of investment, then as a senior internet consultant at MCI.
notes: Active in crypto circles and on X; reachable via Fenbushi. Avoid the 2022 personal-wallet hack topic. X/LinkedIn handles come from a crypto wiki, so verify before use.

name: Anne Dinning
current_role: Managing Director and Executive Committee member, D. E. Shaw group
profile: Seattle-born computer scientist (UW BS, NYU Courant PhD) who joined D. E. Shaw in 1990 as a quant researcher building models for Japanese stocks, and has been on the executive committee running the firm day to day since 2002. Her stake in the quant giant underpins her fortune; she has given over $300M to her Corabelle Lumps Foundation and serves on the boards of Robin Hood and Math for America.
interesting_fact: When she joined D. E. Shaw in 1990 the firm reportedly had about 20 employees, working in a loft with unfinished ceilings and exposed pipes.
deep_cut_fact: Her UW senior thesis was a text editor designed for DeafBlind users, built with Prof. Richard Ladner; she later co-endowed (with husband Michael Wolf) a UW professorship named for Ladner.
notes: Low public profile but speaks on women in CS/STEM (Code.org board, MIT EECS advisory board). Best route is D. E. Shaw corporate communications or via her CS-education philanthropy.

name: Yuequn Tao
current_role: Chairman, Ovctek China (欧普康视, SZSE: 300595), Hefei
profile: Tao Yuequn (陶悦群) is a physicist-turned-entrepreneur who founded Ovctek in Hefei in 2001, building China's leading maker of orthokeratology (ortho-k) myopia-control contact lenses plus a chain of optometry clinics. He earned an engineering PhD in the US (Forbes says USC; China Daily says UCLA, 1994) and taught at Cal State before returning to China.
interesting_fact: Ovctek describes itself as China's first listed optometry-technology company and runs what it calls the world's largest R&D and production centre for orthokeratology lenses.
deep_cut_fact: He began in nuclear fusion research after a 1984 USTC/CAS master's (he recalls spending two years just getting one program to run); Ovctek started by chance when a friend in China asked him to find ortho-k lenses in the US.
notes: PhD school conflicts between sources (USC per Forbes, UCLA per China Daily/ifeng); avoid naming it. Approach via Ovctek board secretary/IR (listed on SZSE disclosures).

name: Ou Zonghong
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Ronshine China Holdings (HKEX: 3301)
profile: Ou Zonghong (歐宗洪), 56, founded Rongxin (Fujian) Investment in 2003, which became Shanghai-headquartered Ronshine China, a residential property developer listed in Hong Kong. He started out building highways in his native Putian, Fujian, before moving into real estate in 2000; he still leads Ronshine as it works through China's property downturn.
interesting_fact: He began with Putian Transport Engineering, a motorway-construction company he set up in 1995, and moved into property in 2000 via a transport-linked real-estate company.
deep_cut_fact: He has served as a director of Renmin University of China since October 2011, and was named one of Fujian's 'Excellent Entrepreneurs' in 2011 and 2014.
notes: Ronshine defaulted on offshore bonds in 2022 and is in debt restructuring; avoid financial topics. Son Ou Guofei chaired affiliate Ronshine Service. Low media profile; IR email is the only published route.

name: Nezih Barut
current_role: Chairman, Abdi İbrahim İlaç (Türkiye's largest pharmaceutical company)
profile: A 1976 Istanbul University pharmacy graduate, Barut joined Abdi İbrahim (founded 1912 as a pharmacy by Abdi İbrahim Barut) the same year and has run the family company since 1981, institutionalising and internationalising it into Türkiye's top drugmaker. He is a long-time chairman of the pharma manufacturers' association İEİS, invests in startups via Revo Capital, and is a Fenerbahçe board figure.
interesting_fact: He has led Abdi İbrahim for over four decades, having worked up through roles such as production manager and general manager after joining in 1976.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he became the first Turkish businessman awarded the Prince Henrik honorary medal by the Danish Export Association.
notes: Fluent English speaker per his İEİS CV. Also partner in Revo Capital (Turkish VC) and was named a Fenerbahçe vice president. Route via Abdi İbrahim corporate communications or İEİS.

name: Ali Parsadoust
current_role: Founder & CEO, Quadrivia AI (AI assistant 'Qu' for clinicians)
profile: Ali Parsa (Parsadoust), born 1965 in Rasht, Iran, is a UCL-trained engineer and ex-investment banker (CSFB, Merrill Lynch, Goldman Sachs) who co-founded hospital operator Circle Health in 2004 and digital-health company Babylon Health in 2014, which listed via SPAC in 2021 and collapsed in 2023. In 2024 he launched Quadrivia, backed by Norrsken, building an AI assistant for doctors.
interesting_fact: Circle Health, which he set up in 2004, became the first private company to run an NHS hospital (Hinchingbrooke) and was structured as a large partnership of clinicians.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Iran in 1981 he taught himself O- and A-levels, and while doing his UCL PhD co-founded media-promotion firm Victoria & Gilan, winning a Royal Award for Young Entrepreneur of the Year in 1993.
notes: Babylon's 2023 collapse wiped out his paper fortune; likely no longer a billionaire. Avoid Babylon/Hinchingbrooke failures. Speaks publicly (Slush 2025, London Tech Week). Reportedly Spain-resident. Best route: Quadrivia.
